facts.rationale: Replaces the erroneous characterization of the guarded hitbox operation as chain cleanup.
facts.value: Calls ft_80081D0C and dispatches no local transition on zero. On nonzero it invokes ftSk_SpecialS_80111EB4, entering aerial ending state 354 from active aerial state 353. Entry resets x0, activates and resets the four hitbox records only when x1C != 0, installs damage/death cleanup callbacks only when the Chain pointer exists, and unconditionally restores accessory and hitlag callbacks. It always forwards gobj to ftSk_SpecialS_80110788, which derives current-minus-previous stick deltas, updates directional sound cooldowns, and optionally attenuates the deltas using the Chain article threshold. The aerial animation callback later consumes and clears x4 after its strict duration guard.

facts.rationale: Corrects the stale held_inputs field spelling and preserves the complete supported flow.
facts.value: Reads HSD_PAD_B from fp->input.held_buttons[0] and sets fp->mv.sk.specials.x4 when B is absent. It always calls ftSk_SpecialS_80110788 with gobj; that helper derives current-minus-previous stick deltas, updates directional sound cooldowns, and optionally attenuates both delta axes using the retained Chain article's threshold. The grounded animation callback later reads x4 with the incremented timer and attribute x14, clears it on a permitted exit, and enters grounded ending state 351.

facts.rationale: Preserves exceptional helper effects and the grounded entry's additional branch.
facts.value: Calls the shared startup helper on each update. A false result causes no further dispatch by this wrapper, but does not guarantee the fighter remains in startup: the helper can already have selected Fall or the common grounded exit after spawn failure. A true result, determined by x0 > attribute x20 after increment, invokes grounded active entry ftSk_SpecialS_80111830. That entry selects state 350, resets x0, and may immediately enter grounded ending state 351 if its environment probe returns nonzero.

facts.rationale: Corrects zero-only cooldown eligibility and preserves exact branch ordering.
facts.value: Computes stick deltas first and maintains two independent sound cooldowns. Positive x8 decrements; otherwise a facing-relative forward delta beyond 0.3 plays the first sound and sets x8 to 6, or an upward delta above 0.5 plays that sound and sets x8 to 12. Positive xC decrements; otherwise, including negative xC, a facing-relative backward delta beyond 0.3 with the current stick behind Sheik plays the second sound and sets xC to 6. A null Chain skips only the final attenuation. With a Chain, both stored delta axes are halved only when both current axis magnitudes are strictly below article x48.

facts.rationale: Corrects the baseline's reversed active-versus-ending call-site classification.
facts.value: Every invocation processes all four fighter hitbox records with lbColl_80008434, clears their x58 and x4C vectors, and sets x2219_b3. The routine has no gameplay guard itself. Grounded and aerial active entries invoke it unconditionally after selecting states 350 and 353; both ending entries invoke it only when move-local x1C != 0 after selecting states 351 and 354.

facts.rationale: The probe's callee selects grounded ending state 351.
facts.value: Implements entry into the grounded deployed-control phase of Sheik's Chain. It prepares the fighter pose, hitboxes, and article callbacks, then uses an initial environment probe to decide whether to begin grounded retraction immediately. The probe does not convert the move to its aerial active phase.

facts.rationale: Replaces the unsupported aerial-conversion interpretation with the actual destination.
facts.value: Enters grounded active Chain state 350, initializes pose selector 305 at transition weight zero, resets the phase timer, activates/resets four hitboxes, and installs article lifecycle, accessory, and hitlag callbacks. It then probes from the world-space ECB vertical midpoint to FtPart_L3rdNa with parameter 0.5; a nonzero result invokes grounded ending entry ftSk_SpecialS_80111DF8.

facts.rationale: Corrects destination semantics without losing ordered initialization or conditional callbacks.
facts.value: Unconditionally selects state 350 at frame 0, speed 1, flags 8; applies pose setup (305, 0), resets x0, and activates/resets hitboxes. Damage/death callbacks are installed only if the Chain exists; x2222_b2 and accessory/hitlag callbacks are always set. After setup, any nonzero environment-probe result invokes the same grounded ending entry used by active grounded collision failure, selecting state 351 rather than an aerial active state.

facts.rationale: Corrects the claim that the countdown itself is forwarded.
facts.value: Passes gobj to Fighter_ChangeMotionState for state 351, resolves the Fighter, and writes x0 = 0. It tests move-local x1C != 0 and, when true, passes gobj—not the countdown—to ftSk_SpecialS_80110AEC for four-hitbox activation/reset. It tests u.sk.x8 before installing damage/death cleanup callbacks, then sets x2222_b2 and the accessory, pre-hitlag, and post-hitlag callback slots.

facts.rationale: Preserves the independent expiry path and the actual item-side exceptional flag branch.
facts.value: Does nothing when the retained Chain pointer is null. Otherwise it forwards the item to it_802BAF0C and sets move-local x20 to 2. Subsequent collision updates decrement x20 only on the low-movement path and use its nonpositive value to permit that path's clearing. This grace does not prevent the independent positive-x1C countdown from reaching zero and clearing collisions first. The item wrapper reaches it_8026B73C, which conditionally sets x5 when x7 is set and clears x3 when set.

facts.rationale: Accounts for cross-file reentrant cleanup instead of assuming the article remains live after removal.
facts.value: Resolves the Fighter and returns immediately if u.sk.x8 is null. Otherwise it passes that item to it_802BB20C. Item removal invokes ftSk_SpecialS_80110E4C on an existing owner before clearing item ownership and deleting links; that owner reset performs post-hitlag notification while the item is still tracked and then clears the fighter pointer and damage/death callbacks. After removal returns, the outer routine resolves fighter data again, calls ftSk_SpecialS_ChainSomething, and clears the same fields. In the normal owner path, this later helper sees null and does not issue a second item notification.

facts.rationale: Corrects the lifecycle explanation while retaining the supported cleanup purpose.
facts.value: Conditionally removes Sheik's tracked Chain article and clears its fighter-side ownership and damage/death cleanup callbacks. Removal includes an item-to-owner reset callback before article deletion, so the normal lifecycle performs post-hitlag notification during that reset, not by dereferencing a still-live article after removal returns.

facts.rationale: Corrects the claimed driver of subsequent setup.
facts.value: Unconditionally enters grounded startup state 349 at frame 0 and speed 1 with flags 0, advances animation initialization, and resets shared Chain working state. The installed accessory4 callback is empty. Timed article creation is driven later by ftSk_SpecialSStart_Anim through ftSk_SpecialS_CheckInitChain, not by the accessory callback.

evidence.why: Consumer guards its owner before calling.

facts.rationale: Preserves the exact textual branch while making the valid-object precondition explicit.
facts.value: Read-only fighter-to-item lifetime predicate with signature bool(HSD_GObj*). For a valid Sheik fighter, returns false when u.sk.x4 is nonzero and true when it is zero. The source contains a true-return null-object branch, but resolves Fighter through GET_FIGHTER before testing gobj; the branch does not establish a null-safe API.

facts.rationale: Corrects null semantics without losing the independent producer and consumer flow.
facts.value: Evaluates gobj->user_data before testing gobj and, for a valid fighter object, returns u.sk.x0 unchanged. Its textual zero-return branch is not a null-safe fallback because the dereference precedes it. SpecialN charging increments and caps this stock at six, firing decrements positive stock once per shot, and the held-needle item consumes the accessor result to show or hide six model nodes. The accessor performs no writes.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes normal semantic range and valid-object precondition from unchecked implementation behavior.
facts.value: Read-only int(HSD_GObj*) accessor requiring a valid Sheik fighter object. It returns the persistent Needle Storm stock, normally 0 through 6 under the charging/firing lifecycle, without clamping it. Although the source contains a zero-return branch for gobj == NULL, gobj->user_data is evaluated first, so null input is not supported by that branch.

facts.rationale: Corrects displacement to velocity and preserves failure fallthrough.
facts.value: Advances shared grounded/aerial Chain startup: increments its counter, spawns and retains the Chain at an exact attribute milestone, installs lifecycle and hitlag callbacks, initializes a facing-relative link velocity at the next-count milestone, and reports completion when the counter exceeds attribute x20. Spawn failure selects Fall or the common grounded exit but does not immediately return from this helper.

evidence.why: Milestones, failure routing, and return consumers.
Velocity initialization and item state transition.

facts.rationale: Captures complete ordering, exceptional flow, and independently proved velocity semantics.
facts.value: Increments x0 first. At x0 == attribute x1C, spawns the Chain, stores its result in u.sk.x8 and x1984_heldItemSpec, installs damage/death callbacks only on success, installs hitlag callbacks regardless, and initializes move-local x1C from attribute x18. A null spawn selects Fall in air or the common grounded exit otherwise, without an immediate return. At x0 == attribute x1C + 1, an unchecked item dereference obtains article x50 and sends (item-facing*x50, 0, 0) to the link-velocity initializer. Finally returns x0 > attribute x20; callers dispatch their active entries on true. Milestones use exact equality rather than catch-up comparisons.

evidence.why: Registered startup, active, and ending callback suites.
Active input, animation, collision, and entry.
Ending milestones, conversions, and guarded activation.

facts.rationale: Corrects the baseline's shifted phase mapping and conventional-swap assumption using canonical entries and callback registration.
facts.value: Chain's ground/aerial startup states are 349/352, active states 350/353, and ending states 351/354. Startup animation drives exact spawn and link-velocity milestones and enters active state after a strict completion threshold. Active IASA latches B release; animation enters same-form ending after the strict minimum-duration guard. Active collision also enters same-form ending, and the grounded active-entry environment probe can immediately enter 351. Startup and ending situation-conversion helpers preserve their phase and retained article while restoring callbacks. Ending entry activation is guarded by x1C != 0 in both forms; ending animation uses exact item milestones and separately handles animation completion.
